newsitem.title: UK: Yorkshire Water lifts hosepipe bans.
newsitem.headline: Yorkshire Water lifts hosepipe bans.

text.p: Yorkshire Water said on Tuesday it will lift the hosepipe bans and other water restrictions from November 1 after the fiercely criticised measures came into force during the 1995 summer drought.
The completion of schemes to secure water supplies in Yorkshire and access to the Kielder Reservoir in Northumberland in times of shortage had made the restictitions superfluous.
"We now have a strong and expanded Yorkshire grid, able to move more water on a much wider scale in the region," said Brandon Gough, Yorkshire Water's chairman.
Gough added that the utility would no longer have to bring water into the region through an intensive lorry service as started in November last year.

"Should we have a repeat of the weather conditions of 1995, we will not have to resort to the tankering or the threat of rota cuts or standpipes as experienced in West Yorkshire last year," Gough said.
Yorkshire Water said it would continue to make extra efforts to reduce leakages after critics last year accused it of having spent insufficient money in maintainance of its pipelines.
